claims.claim: Toronto police charged Florin Mitea, 34, with dangerous operation causing death and bodily harm and obstructing a peace officer, and Gabriel Mitea, 25, with obstructing a peace officer, over an October 11 Scarborough collision.
A 68-year-old woman passenger in the Ford Escape died in hospital after the October 11 crash at Lawrence Avenue East and Scarborough Golf Club Road.
TPS lists the second accused as 25 while CBC reports 24.
Gabriel Mitea is scheduled to appear at Ontario Court of Justice on December 23.
A man approached a person in the Eglinton Avenue East and Yonge Street area on October 9, claimed to be a Spiritual Holistic Healer and sexually assaulted the victim during a reading, police say.
The suspect is described as 50 to 60 years old, medium build, long black and grey hair in a black dew rag, full beard.

The College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario board approved requiring safer supply prescriptions only with opioid agonist therapy and consumption in front of a health-care professional, and dropped the eight-week limit.

claims.claim: CP24 reports 225,550 advance voters and a single-day record of 53,363 on October 11; the City of Toronto's figure recorded earlier is 222,550.
Election day is Monday, October 26, with polls open 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.
No implementation date for the safer supply changes is stated in the reports.
It is not established whether Syed Raza appeared at the Toronto Regional Bail Centre on October 11.

claims.claim: A Nanos Poll for CP24 and CTV News Toronto, surveyed Oct. 8-10 among 757 residents, puts Chow at 51 per cent and Bradford at 47 per cent among decided voters, a lead of about 3.5 points.
claims.attributed_to: Nanos Polling for CP24 and CTV News Toronto

claims.claim: The City of Toronto says 222,550 voters cast advance ballots over six days, Oct. 6-11, a record since 2010 and up about 92 per cent from 2022.
Election day is Monday, Oct. 26, with polls open 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.

Paul Conn, 71, of Toronto, was arrested and charged with five counts of sexual assault, three counts of sexual interference with a person under 16, and four counts of sexual exploitation of a young person.

Police allege Conn met the victim while working at a church in the Bloor Street West and Kipling Avenue area and assaulted the victim multiple times between 2021 and 2026 while the victim was a youth.
Conn was scheduled to appear at the Toronto Regional Bail Centre on Tuesday, Oct. 13, at 9:30 a.m. in room 107.
